setup: The PDF split-and-merge application is installed and opened in its graphical interface, with no document currently modified.
action: The user loads one or more PDF files into the tool and inspects the available document actions.
expected_observation: The application presents a free graphical workspace for PDF manipulation, and the loaded source PDFs remain unchanged on disk unless the user explicitly creates a new output file.

setup: The user has a PDF document with multiple pages loaded into the graphical workspace.
action: The user chooses the split operation and specifies a split point or page range to divide the document into separate files.
expected_observation: The system creates separate PDF output files according to the selected split rule, and each resulting file contains the expected subset of pages.

setup: Two or more PDF files, or selected page sections from PDF files, are loaded into the workspace and ready for combination.
action: The user selects the desired PDFs or page sections and triggers the merge operation.
expected_observation: The system generates a single combined PDF in the chosen order, containing all selected files or sections as one merged document.

setup: A multi-page PDF is loaded and the user can view its page thumbnails or page list.
action: The user selects one or more pages to extract into a new document and confirms the extraction.
expected_observation: The system produces a new PDF containing only the selected pages, with the original document still available unchanged.

setup: A PDF document with pages in a known orientation is loaded into the workspace.
action: The user rotates one or more selected pages by a chosen angle and applies the operation.
expected_observation: The selected pages are shown in the new orientation in the output PDF, while the source PDF remains unchanged.

setup: A PDF document with multiple pages is loaded and its page order is visible in the workspace.
action: The user reorders pages by dragging them into a new sequence and confirms the change.
expected_observation: The resulting PDF reflects the new page order exactly as arranged by the user.

setup: Two PDF documents are loaded, each containing pages intended to be interleaved in a defined alternating pattern.
action: The user selects an alternating merge pattern between the two documents and executes the operation.
expected_observation: The generated PDF alternates pages from the selected documents according to the chosen pattern, producing a single interleaved output.

setup: The user has opened multiple PDF files and is viewing their page thumbnails in the graphical workspace.
action: The user visually assembles a new document by dragging selected pages into a composition area and arranging them in the desired layout and order.
expected_observation: The system creates a new PDF that matches the composed arrangement shown in the workspace, including the selected pages and their visual order.

setup: A source PDF file exists on disk, and the user begins a document operation such as split, merge, extract, or rotate.
action: The user completes the operation normally, and then repeats the action with an error condition such as canceling the save location or providing invalid input.
expected_observation: In both the successful and failed cases, the original PDF input file remains byte-for-byte unchanged on disk, and only new output files or no files are created as appropriate.

setup: The user has configured a PDF operation workspace with selected files, page selections, and transformation settings.
action: The user saves the workspace or job configuration under a reusable name and later opens that saved configuration.
expected_observation: The saved workspace is restored with the same document selections and operation settings, allowing the user to repeat the same job without reconfiguring it manually.

setup: A user is on a system where scripted or repeated PDF manipulation tasks must be run without using the graphical interface.
action: The user invokes the command-line interface with arguments that define a PDF operation such as split, merge, or extract.
expected_observation: The system executes the requested PDF operation from the command line and produces the expected output without requiring interaction with the graphical tool.

setup: The graphical application is open and the user has access to file loading and document operation controls in the same session.
action: The user loads one or more PDFs and immediately performs an operation such as extracting pages or merging sections without opening a separate application.
expected_observation: The system supports the entire workflow within one interface session, with the loaded files, selected pages, and operation results available without switching to another tool.

setup: The user has selected a valid PDF manipulation action and chosen an output destination.
action: The user confirms the operation to generate the final document.
expected_observation: The system creates a new output PDF file representing the manipulated result of the job.

setup: A source PDF file is loaded and a final output filename and location are available for saving the result.
action: The user saves the final manipulated PDF to a new file name or destination.
expected_observation: The output PDF is written to the chosen location, and the original source PDF files are not overwritten or altered.

setup: A batch job is prepared with several PDF files, including a mix of valid files and at least one file that is invalid, unreadable, or unsupported, and continuing with safe valid files is possible.
action: The user starts batch processing with the option to continue when safe.
expected_observation: The system processes the valid files in the batch, skips or reports the invalid file(s), and continues only where it is safe to do so without stopping the entire batch.

setup: A batch merge job has already been run in the PDF Split and Merge application, and at least one item in the batch failed because one source PDF was temporarily unavailable or corrupted. The failed job entry is visible in the batch history with its error status.
action: The user fixes the underlying issue by restoring the missing PDF file or replacing the damaged input, then selects only the failed batch items and chooses the option to rerun failed items.
expected_observation: Only the previously failed batch items are executed again, the successful items are not rerun, and the job history updates to show the retried items completing successfully or reporting any remaining errors individually.

setup: The user has an active workspace open with a prepared document arrangement, including loaded PDFs, split or merge settings, and selected output options. A batch item fails because one input path or setting is incorrect, but the workspace remains open.
action: The user corrects the incorrect input or setting directly in the current workspace and retries the operation without creating a new workspace or re-importing all documents.
expected_observation: The original workspace layout, loaded documents, and configured job settings are preserved, allowing the user to retry immediately from the same screen without rebuilding the setup from scratch.

setup: The application is open on the start screen or workspace screen, and the user has access to saved workspace, preset, or job files stored locally.
action: The user opens the import wizard and selects a saved workspace, preset, or job file to bring into the application.
expected_observation: An import wizard appears and guides the user through loading the selected file, showing the imported item as a workspace, preset, or job ready for review before it is added to the application.

setup: The user has opened the import wizard and selected a workflow or settings file to import, including either a valid file or one containing unsupported or malformed entries.
action: The user proceeds to the validation step in the import wizard.
expected_observation: The system checks the imported file before completing the import and clearly reports validation errors, warnings, or pass status so the user can decide whether to continue or correct the file.

setup: The import wizard has loaded a saved workflow, preset, or job definition that can be reviewed before import completion.
action: The user advances to the review stage of the import wizard.
expected_observation: The wizard displays a preview or side-by-side comparison of the imported workflow details, allowing the user to compare the incoming configuration with the current or default settings before finalizing.

setup: A workflow, preset, or job file has been imported into the import wizard and is currently shown in the review or edit stage before being saved.
action: The user edits one or more imported settings, such as output folder, page range, or merge options, and then chooses to save the import.
expected_observation: The edited values are retained in the imported job or configuration, and the saved result reflects the user's changes rather than the original imported values.

setup: The user imports a workflow or settings file that contains a mix of supported settings and unsupported items from another tool or older version.
action: The user completes the import process.
expected_observation: The system imports the parts it understands, explicitly lists unsupported items or skipped settings, and completes the import without stopping silently or discarding the entire workflow.

setup: The user is migrating a workspace from an older PDF tool, and the imported file contains legacy terminology that does not match the new application's current naming, such as old labels for split rules, output targets, or job actions.
action: The user runs the migration import and opens the terminology mapping step or prompt.
expected_observation: The system shows how old terminology maps to the new tool's terms, helping the user understand which legacy options correspond to the current configuration names before import is finalized.

setup: During import, the wizard detects an issue such as an unsupported field, missing file, or ambiguous workflow setting.
action: The user continues through the import wizard while the issue is present.
expected_observation: The wizard provides inline guidance next to the problem area, explaining the issue in context and indicating what the user can change or review before proceeding.

setup: The application is ready to assist with migration or common import tasks, and the user is not familiar with the import format or workspace transfer process.
action: The user opens the help content from the import or migration screen.
expected_observation: The system displays plain-language help that explains common import and migration scenarios in simple terms, including what to do when bringing in saved workspaces, presets, or job files.

setup: The user is working on a computer with local files available on the file system, and the application has access to standard open and save dialogs.
action: The user selects a local PDF as input and chooses a local folder or file path as the output destination for a split or merge operation.
expected_observation: The application successfully reads input from the local file system and writes output to the specified local location, confirming the local path-based operation without requiring a cloud or network location.

setup: The graphical interface is open on a screen with interactive controls such as menus, buttons, lists, and text fields.
action: The user moves through the interface using only the keyboard, including Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys, Enter, and Space.
expected_observation: Focus moves in a logical order through actionable controls, menus and buttons can be activated from the keyboard, and the user can complete core tasks without using a mouse.

setup: A screen reader is enabled on the user's computer and the PDF Split and Merge interface is open.
action: The user navigates through the interface controls and dialogs with the screen reader active.
expected_observation: Controls, labels, dialog titles, statuses, and warnings are announced in a meaningful way, allowing the user to understand and operate the interface without relying on visual cues.

setup: The application is displaying its main interface, including form fields, toolbars, buttons, and informational text under normal visual settings.
action: The user views the interface in a standard lighting environment and inspects key controls and text labels.
expected_observation: Text and controls are clearly distinguishable from the background, important UI elements have readable labels, and the interface maintains sufficient contrast for practical use.

setup: The user has enabled larger text or accessibility display settings on the operating system, and the application is open with a simplified or responsive layout available.
action: The user increases text size and continues using the application to access common split, merge, or import screens.
expected_observation: The interface remains usable with enlarged text, key controls stay visible and understandable, and the layout adapts or simplifies enough to avoid critical overlap, truncation, or loss of functionality.

setup: A PDF split job is open in the workspace and one selected source file has a missing or unreadable page reference that prevents the job from continuing for that specific file.
action: The user starts the split operation for the configured job.
expected_observation: An inline error message appears directly beside the affected file or page entry, identifying exactly which file or page has the problem, while the rest of the workspace remains visible.

setup: A merge job is configured with one source PDF that is corrupted and cannot be opened, causing the job to be blocked from starting.
action: The user clicks the command to run the merge job.
expected_observation: A blocking pop-up message appears explaining that the job cannot proceed because the selected file is unreadable, and any related file-level issue is also shown inline in the workspace where appropriate.

setup: A batch split workspace contains several selected PDFs, page ranges, and output settings, and one page range is invalid so the job fails validation.
action: The user attempts to run the batch job and then dismisses the error message.
expected_observation: The current workspace remains unchanged, including selected files, page ranges, and output settings, so the user can correct the invalid entry and retry without rebuilding the job.

setup: A large merge job involving many PDF files has been started and is expected to take several minutes to complete.
action: The user begins the job and watches the job status area during processing.
expected_observation: A visible progress indicator shows the job advancing over time, such as percentage complete, current file being processed, or a progress bar that updates until the job finishes.

setup: One long-running PDF merge job is already running in the background while the main workspace is still available for creating another job.
action: The user continues working in the interface, opens a second split job, and submits it to the job queue.
expected_observation: The interface remains responsive, the second job is accepted into the queue or background processing area, and the user can still navigate the workspace without the application appearing frozen.

setup: Several jobs are queued, and queue controls such as pause, resume, and reorder are available because the current job list supports background execution.
action: The user pauses a queued job, resumes it later, and changes the order of two queued jobs by moving one above the other.
expected_observation: The paused job stops advancing, the resumed job continues processing, and the queue order updates to match the user's requested priority.

setup: The user has an exported workspace or preset file created by another compatible PDF split-and-merge tool, containing saved job settings and file selections.
action: The user imports the saved workspace or preset into the application.
expected_observation: The application loads the compatible settings into a new workspace or preset view, preserving the recognizable job configuration where supported and indicating any unsupported elements clearly.

setup: A PDF is opened in the application for a split-and-merge workflow.
action: The user looks for tools to edit text, retouch images, annotate pages, or redesign page content inside the opened PDF.
expected_observation: The application does not provide full document-editing capabilities such as text rewriting or image editing, and only split, merge, or related job controls are available.

setup: A merge job is in progress and one input file triggers an error while the application is processing it.
action: The error occurs and the user inspects the source PDF afterward in its original folder.
expected_observation: The original file remains unchanged on disk, with no edits, replacements, or partial modifications made during error handling.

setup: The user is preparing output for a team with its own established folder structure and naming convention, such as project-based folders and date-stamped filenames.
action: The user configures the output location and filename for a split or merge job.
expected_observation: The application allows the user to save outputs into the existing team folder structure and naming pattern without requiring a special proprietary directory layout.

setup: A batch job includes multiple PDFs, and the user is prompted to choose how the system should behave if one file fails.
action: The user selects the option to stop on the first error or the option to continue processing after errors, then runs the batch job.
expected_observation: The batch behavior follows the selected rule: either processing stops immediately at the first failure or it continues with the remaining eligible files.

setup: The application is installed on a laptop with no network connection available.
action: The user launches the application and processes a local PDF split or merge job.
expected_observation: The job can be configured and executed offline using local files, with no requirement to sign in or contact a remote service for normal processing.

setup: A split or merge job has been completed or canceled, and temporary working files were created during processing.
action: The user checks the application's temporary file location after the job ends or is canceled.
expected_observation: Temporary files are removed automatically, leaving no leftover intermediate processing files from the finished or canceled job.

setup: A regular user is saving a workspace or output file, and the organization policy does not require encryption for that environment.
action: The user saves the workspace or generated PDF and reviews available save options.
expected_observation: Encryption is available as an optional choice for the regular user. In a managed or enterprise environment where policy requires it, encrypted saving is enforced and the user cannot bypass the policy.

setup: A workspace has been saved and contains source file paths, merge order, page selections, and other workflow details that could reveal sensitive information.
action: The user reviews the saved workspace protection settings or attempts to save it without protection.
expected_observation: The workspace is protected using security controls at least equivalent to those used for output files, so workspace data is not stored with weaker protection than the generated PDFs.

setup: A user is preparing sensitive PDF work in the desktop application and has selected an output location for a merged or split document.
action: The user enables password protection for the generated PDF and chooses a modern encryption option offered by the application.
expected_observation: The application creates a password-protected PDF using the selected modern encryption method and confirms that the protected output was generated successfully.

setup: The application is being used in a team or regulated environment where audit logging has been enabled by an administrator.
action: A user performs a PDF split or merge operation that generates one or more output files.
expected_observation: An audit trail entry is recorded for the operation and is available to authorized reviewers in the environment's audit log.

setup: Audit trail capture is enabled in a regulated workspace and the user is signed in to the application.
action: The user runs a PDF merge operation that completes successfully.
expected_observation: The audit record includes the user identity, the timestamp, the source file names, the output file name, the operation type, and a success status.

setup: An administrator has enabled the advanced high-security option for stronger protection of temporary files in the application settings.
action: The user starts a PDF split or merge operation that requires temporary working files.
expected_observation: The application stores temporary files using the stronger protection mode and indicates that the high-security temporary-file option is active.

setup: A PDF operation has failed after the user selected an incorrect source file or page range.
action: The user edits the selection, replaces the bad file with a correct one, or reruns the operation from the saved state.
expected_observation: The application allows the user to correct the inputs and retry the task without losing the rest of the configured work.

setup: The selected PDF files or requested operation are known to have practical limits, such as large file size, many pages, or a high number of output documents.
action: The user initiates the split or merge operation with inputs that approach or exceed the practical limit.
expected_observation: Before processing starts, the application communicates the practical limit in clear terms and warns the user about the expected constraint.

setup: The user has access to a local folder containing one or more PDF files and has chosen an output folder on the same machine.
action: The user opens a PDF from the local file system, then saves a split or merged result back to disk.
expected_observation: The application reads the source PDF from the local file system and writes the generated PDF output to the selected local path.

setup: A script or automated workflow is prepared on a workstation with the PDF application installed.
action: The automation invokes the application through its command-line interface to split or merge PDF files.
expected_observation: The application accepts command-line input, performs the requested PDF operation, and returns a script-friendly result indicating success or failure.

setup: The user has a workflow or settings file exported from a previous session or another instance of the application.
action: The user imports the workflow or settings file into the application.
expected_observation: The application loads the imported configuration and applies the workflow or settings to the current session.

setup: The user has completed a PDF operation and has chosen to save the generated files and workspace state.
action: The user saves the split or merged documents together with the workspace for later reuse.
expected_observation: The application produces the output PDF files and a saved workspace artifact that can be reopened later with the preserved state.

setup: A casual user opens the application for the first time without prior training and sees the main PDF split-and-merge workspace.
action: The user follows the on-screen controls to add files and run a basic split or merge task.
expected_observation: The user can complete the common task using straightforward controls and clear labels without needing advanced instructions.

setup: The user has access to this PDF application and a comparable alternative tool for the same split or merge task.
action: The user compares the steps needed to perform the same routine PDF operation in both tools.
expected_observation: The application requires fewer or simpler steps, with a clearer workflow and less configuration effort than the alternative.

setup: A user needs to repeatedly clean up or assemble PDFs as part of a routine document workflow.
action: The user performs a common split or merge task from start to finish using the application.
expected_observation: The task can be completed in a short, efficient workflow that reduces the time spent on routine PDF cleanup and assembly compared with manual handling.

setup: The user is preparing a PDF merge or split and has several source documents that must remain in a specific order.
action: The user reviews the selected files and runs the operation after arranging the inputs in the intended sequence.
expected_observation: The application preserves the intended order and helps prevent accidental source-file changes or page-order mistakes during the operation.

setup: The application encounters an error while processing a PDF, such as an unreadable file, missing input, or write-permission problem.
action: The user attempts the split or merge operation with the problematic input.
expected_observation: The application stops gracefully and shows a specific, understandable error message that explains the cause and points to the affected file or setting instead of a generic failure.

setup: The PDF Split and Merge application is running a command-line, batch, or automated job with logging enabled and a writable log location configured.
action: The job processes a set of PDF files through a split or merge operation.
expected_observation: The system writes detailed diagnostic logs that include the job start time, input files, operation being performed, progress or step milestones, warnings or errors, and the final result.

setup: The desktop application is open and a large merge or split job has been started from the user interface.
action: The user attempts to move the window, open menus, switch tabs, or cancel the job while processing continues.
expected_observation: The interface remains responsive to user input, controls still react without freezing, and the application window can be moved or interacted with while the job runs.

setup: A typical batch job with a small-to-moderate number of PDF inputs is queued in an environment with normal system resources and no unusual file corruption.
action: The user starts the batch job and waits for completion.
expected_observation: The batch completes in a short time suitable for normal use, typically within a few seconds up to about a minute, and the application reports successful completion without unnecessary delay.

setup: The application is asked to process a very large PDF or a large batch of PDF files that exceeds typical interactive workload size.
action: The user starts the split or merge operation on the large workload.
expected_observation: The application continues processing without freezing, remains usable for basic interaction, and provides a graceful indication of heavy workload such as progress updates, queued processing, or reduced-speed but stable operation.

setup: The system has moderate batches and larger jobs available for processing, with the user interface open and ready for work.
action: The user starts several jobs of increasing size, including a moderate batch and a larger batch, one after another.
expected_observation: The application scales through the workload without becoming unresponsive, does not lock up during processing, and continues to accept basic UI actions while the jobs complete.

setup: A batch job is running with diagnostic logging enabled and one or more files are configured to fail during processing.
action: The batch finishes with at least one failed file and one successful file.
expected_observation: The diagnostics identify the specific file or files that failed, the operation being performed when the failure occurred, and a cause category such as invalid input, unsupported content, or read/write error.

setup: The application is used with keyboard-only navigation, a screen reader, high contrast mode, and enlarged text settings enabled.
action: The user navigates through the main split and merge workflow using only the keyboard and reads the controls and status messages through the assistive technology.
expected_observation: All primary controls are reachable by keyboard, labels are announced clearly by the screen reader, text remains readable in high contrast and larger text modes, and the workflow can be completed without requiring a mouse.

setup: The user has opened a split or merge dialog and selected an invalid input, such as a missing file, unsupported format, or output location that cannot be written.
action: The user attempts to start the operation with the invalid configuration.
expected_observation: The application shows a plain, specific error message that names the problem in user terms and provides next-step guidance, such as choosing a valid file, selecting a writable folder, or removing the unsupported item.

setup: The workflow editor is open with several PDF files already added as items in the composition area.
action: The user drags files to reorder them, inserts a new file between existing items, and removes one item from the sequence.
expected_observation: The visual workflow updates immediately to reflect the new document order, item placement is shown clearly, and the user can see the composition sequence before running the merge or split job.

setup: A long-running split, merge, or batch operation is in progress.
action: The user watches the operation screen while processing continues.
expected_observation: The system provides ongoing progress feedback such as percentage complete, current file name, step name, or estimated remaining time so the user can tell that work is advancing.

setup: The user imports a document or workflow from an older version, another PDF tool, or a legacy configuration that includes items not fully supported by the current application.
action: The user completes the import process.
expected_observation: The application reports what was preserved, what was converted, and what was not supported, with a clear summary of any lost or ignored elements so the user understands the migration result.

setup: The application is installed on a desktop system managed by IT support, and standard support tools such as logs, configuration files, and version information are available.
action: A support technician opens the application, checks version and settings information, and reviews logs after a reported issue.
expected_observation: The application provides clear versioning, accessible logs, understandable configuration settings, and straightforward troubleshooting information that helps IT or desktop support diagnose and maintain the system.

setup: A batch job contains several valid PDF files and one corrupt or unreadable file.
action: The user starts the batch split or merge operation with the mixed set of files.
expected_observation: The system keeps the valid files in the job intact where possible, processes them successfully, and reports the bad file separately without discarding the rest of the batch.

setup: The user has selected multiple input files, including both valid PDFs and one file that cannot be processed safely.
action: The user starts the multi-file operation.
expected_observation: The system continues with the valid files when it is safe to do so, skips or isolates the problematic file, and reports which file could not be processed along with the reason.

setup: An import package contains a mix of supported document elements and unsupported items such as legacy annotations, uncommon metadata, or obsolete workflow features.
action: The user imports the package into the current application.
expected_observation: The system completes the import for supported content, keeps the rest of the import usable, and reports the unsupported items clearly so the user knows what was not brought across.

setup: The PDF Split and Merge application is open on the workstation, and the user is on the export or save workflow for a completed PDF output.
action: The user looks for built-in options to send the output PDF directly to email, a document management system, or a cloud storage service.
expected_observation: The application does not present any guaranteed integration workflow for email, DMS, or cloud services as a required feature; only the currently available local save or export options are shown, and the absence of these integrations is treated as unresolved rather than an error.

setup: The user has finished configuring a PDF output that includes sensitive content and is at the final save/export step.
action: The user checks the available security or encryption settings for the generated PDF before saving.
expected_observation: The application does not expose a fixed, mandatory encryption standard as a confirmed requirement; if encryption options are present, they are presented as configurable choices rather than a single prescribed method, and no specific standard is assumed by the workflow.

setup: The application is being used in a normal desktop session by a standard user account that creates and saves PDFs.
action: The user completes a split or merge operation and then reviews whether the application automatically records an audit trail for that activity.
expected_observation: The system does not assume that audit trails are mandatory for every user action because that requirement is unresolved; audit logging may be present or absent depending on configuration, but no universal enforcement is asserted by the acceptance behavior.

setup: The user has generated an output PDF and saved a workspace layout for a split/merge task.
action: The user attempts to determine how long the output PDF and the saved workspace setup will remain available before archival or deletion.
expected_observation: The application does not enforce a confirmed retention or archival period as a required behavior; no fixed expiry, retention notification, or automatic archival schedule is assumed, and the lifetime of saved artifacts remains undefined.

setup: The application is ready to process PDF files for a split or merge job.
action: The user prepares a job with a large document, many input files, or a high number of pages and starts the operation without any documented numeric limit being provided.
expected_observation: The system does not present a verified hard limit for file size, page count, or batch size as part of the confirmed acceptance behavior; any limit handling is dependent on product constraints not yet defined, rather than on a fixed requirement.

setup: The desktop application is open, and one user session is actively editing a PDF split or merge workspace.
action: A second user attempts to work on the same workspace or job from another desktop session at the same time.
expected_observation: The application does not guarantee true multi-user concurrent collaboration as a confirmed requirement; simultaneous access behavior is not treated as a mandated capability, and any conflict, blocking, or session separation behavior remains unspecified.

setup: The job queue contains multiple pending PDF split or merge tasks in the desktop application.
action: The user checks whether the queue supports pausing a job, resuming it later, or reordering queued jobs.
expected_observation: The application does not treat pause, resume, or reorder controls as mandatory queue behaviors because they are only a nice-to-have; if such controls are available, they are optional enhancements rather than required acceptance criteria.
